tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Balance, hourly spend, how long the balance lasts, servers against the account limit.

tools.name: list_options
tools.description: Plans with vCPU, RAM, disk, traffic, GPU, hourly and monthly price and the locations they deploy in, cheapest first. Filter by product, provider, location, GPU model and price.

tools.name: list_locations
tools.description: Data center locations with codes, cities and countries.

tools.name: list_os
tools.description: OS images with versions and one-click apps you can deploy.

tools.name: quote
tools.description: Price of an order and whether the balance covers the first hour.

tools.name: create_server
tools.description: Create 1 to 3 servers (OS or one-click app) and charge the first hour. Refuses and returns the price when the total is above max_hourly_usd (default $1/h).

tools.name: list_servers
tools.description: All servers with status, IPs, plan and an ssh command.

tools.name: get_server
tools.description: One server with its current status and addresses.

tools.name: server_power
tools.description: Power actions. A stopped server is still billed.

tools.name: get_root_password
tools.description: The login and root password of a server (stays in the chat history).

tools.name: reset_root_password
tools.description: Set a new password for the server's login user without a reinstall, through the server's recovery key (Linux on Vultr, DigitalOcean, Linode). Random unless password is given. The server must be running.

tools.name: change_ip
tools.description: Give a Vultr server a new IPv4, same data. Small fee and a cooldown. Needs confirm and the exact name.

tools.name: destroy_server
tools.description: Delete a server and its disk; billing stops. Needs confirm=true and the exact name.

tools.name: get_rdns
tools.description: Current PTR records of the server's IPv4 and IPv6.

tools.name: set_rdns
tools.description: Set the PTR record of one of the server's IPs (Linode requires the name to resolve to the IP first).

tools.name: list_backups
tools.description: Snapshots kept 7 days.

tools.name: create_backup
tools.description: Start a snapshot of a server (pending, then available).

tools.name: restore_backup
tools.description: Create a NEW server from a backup (new IP); respects max_hourly_usd.

tools.name: delete_backup
tools.description: Delete a snapshot. Needs confirm=true and the exact label as name.

tools.name: billing_history
tools.description: Recent top-ups and charges.

tools.name: list_currencies
tools.description: Coins the balance can be topped up with, the minimum in US dollars and VAT. Pass currency (an id) for that coin's exact minimum.

tools.name: top_up
tools.description: Create a crypto payment for the user to pay: returns the address, the exact amount, the network and the deadline. Nothing is charged until the user sends it. amount_usd is what the balance receives.

tools.name: list_deposits
tools.description: The last 20 top-ups and their status.

tools.name: support_read
tools.description: The account's support chat, newest last (is_staff = our side, the support AI included).

tools.name: support_send
tools.description: Send a message to Neckrez support on the user's behalf (marked as sent by an AI assistant, at most 10 an hour). Replies appear in support_read.

tools.name: deposit_status
tools.description: Check a top-up live; it is credited to the balance as soon as the payment is confirmed.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_root_password, support_read · Private data: list_servers, get_root_password, reset_root_password, get_rdns, set_rdns · Public sink: support_send · Destructive: reset_root_password, destroy_server, delete_backup.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_root_password, support_read · Private data: list_servers, get_root_password, reset_root_password, get_rdns, set_rdns · Public sink: support_send · Destructive: reset_root_password, destroy_server, delete_backup

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
